rendered: The premise does not match the paper. The authors did not run a melt-diffusion step of that long duration. Their sulfur infiltration was a low-temperature isothermal vapor phase process, run at 175 °C[1] for 1 h[2], which gave 35[3] wt % sulfur confined in the micropores. The long melt duration appears only as a drawback of other methods. The authors state that their vapor approach is significantly more scalable and less expensive[4] than other methods that traditionally employ long (>20 h) melt[5] techniques to ensure pore infiltration. The paper gives no separate rationale for a melt step of that length, because it does not use such a step. Its stated reason for choosing isothermal vapor phase infiltration is scalability and lower cost.
